new_task_1.title: Make captured stdin placeholder behave like a text stream
new_task_1.description: When pytest replaces stdin during output capture, the placeholder object now behaves more like a real text stream. It exposes a string encoding derived from the real stdin and supports context-manager usage, while continuing to reject read attempts with the existing OSError and write attempts with UnsupportedOperation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Some code interacting with sys.stdin during pytest capture expects basic text-stream attributes and protocols, such as a string-valued encoding or support for use in a with-statement. Previously, pytest's captured-stdin placeholder exposed encoding=None and lacked context-manager methods, making it diverge from normal text stream behavior even though it still intentionally forbids reading from stdin under capture.

expectation.grounded: The DontReadFromInput class used for captured stdin must expose an `encoding` property returning `sys.__stdin__.encoding` instead of `None`. It must implement `__enter__` returning itself and `__exit__` as a no-op so it can be used as a context manager. It must continue to raise OSError for `read`, `readline`, `readlines`, and iteration-driven reads, and continue to reject write operations with UnsupportedOperation.
expectation.conceptual: During capture, pytest's stdin replacement should more closely resemble a normal text stream for metadata and protocol compatibility, without permitting actual stdin reads.

constraints.grounded: The existing protection against reading from stdin while capture is active must remain unchanged: read-style APIs still raise OSError with the existing guidance to use `-s`. The object must remain non-writable and non-seekable as before. Context-manager support must not close or otherwise alter the placeholder on exit.
constraints.conceptual: This change should improve compatibility with code that inspects or wraps stdin, but it must not weaken pytest's guard against interactive stdin reads during capture.

behavior: When pytest capture replaces stdin, `sys.stdin.encoding` is exposed as a string instead of `None`.
The captured-stdin placeholder can be used in a `with` statement and yields itself from `__enter__`.
Calling `read`, `readline`, `readlines`, or advancing iteration on the captured-stdin placeholder still raises OSError instructing users to consider `-s`.
Calling `write` or `writelines` on the captured-stdin placeholder still raises UnsupportedOperation.
acceptance_criteria: Under active capture, accessing the replacement stdin object's `encoding` attribute returns a string value.
Using the replacement stdin object in `with sys.stdin:` succeeds without raising and leaves the object usable afterward.
Calling `sys.stdin.read()` under capture still raises OSError with the existing captured-stdin warning.
Calling `sys.stdin.writelines(...)` under capture still raises UnsupportedOperation.
